situation.problem_text:
Topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D

Target audience: University students (STEM majors)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: From 2D to 3D

Lecture lines:
We begin with 2D circles using the Pythagorean theorem.
Generalizing, we move to 3D spheres.
A sphere is the set of points equidistant from center.
Mathematically, x-squared plus y-squared plus z-squared equals r-squared.
Planar slices reveal how dimensions nest within each other.

Planned animations:
Create a 2D circle with center at origin, color #FF00FF.
Add a 3D sphere with same radius, color #00FFFF.
Show overlap area decreasing as dimensions increase.
Fade in text: 'Volume concentration'.
Highlight concentration of volume near the surface.

Section: section_2 — Generalizing to N-Dimensions

Lecture lines:
Now we generalize to N-dimensions, the hypersphere.
The equation follows the same sum-of-squares pattern.
We represent an N-dimensional unit sphere algebraically.

Planned animations:
Display unit N-cube and N-sphere, label both, color #FFFFFF.
Show volume formula comparison, color #FFFF00.
Fade in N=3 visual compared to N=2.
Animate N increasing to show relative volume.
Fade in formula for hypersphere volume.

Section: section_3 — The Counter-Intuitive 'Spiky' Volume

Lecture lines:
High-dimensional volumes behave quite counter-intuitively.
Volume concentrates primarily near the surface or crust.
The core becomes negligible as dimensions increase.
Imagine peeling a 100-dimensional orange.
Most of the volume resides in the skin.

Planned animations:
Display hypercube with spikes at corners, color #FF4500.
Animate increasing dimensions focusing on corner volume.
Highlight 'spiky' shape growing outward, color #00FF00.
Fade in text: 'Empty core', color #FF0000.
Collapse inner region to show volume migration.

Section: section_4 — Application: The Curse of Dimensionality

Lecture lines:
This leads to the curse of dimensionality.
In high dimensions, distance metrics lose their meaning.
Data points effectively migrate to the hypersphere's surface.

Planned animations:
Show a high-dimensional scatter plot, color #AABBCC.
Highlight points moving toward surface, color #EECC33.
Fade in label: 'Distance becomes meaningless'.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Synthesis

Lecture lines:
Hyperspheres are essential extensions of 3D geometry.
They are critical for understanding modern big data.
Their volume distribution challenges our spatial intuition.

Planned animations:
Flash core concepts: N-dimensions, Volume, Concentration, color #FFD700.
Show summary table of key findings, color #FFFFFF.
Fade out all elements to black.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)

        self.add(self.lecture)

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
